To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CFTR corrector, VX-809, increases the binding affinity of ΔF508-CFTR to NHERF1, and that the interaction of ΔF508 with NHERF1 is a determinant of ΔF508 functional efficiency.
the interaction of CFTR with NHERF1 is a determinant of its functional efficiency and that the CFTR corrector, VX-809, potentiates the interaction of NHERF1 with CFTR.
the CFTR-correcting drug VX-809 prolong the stability of the mutant CFTR at plasma membrane by increasing the binding affinity between the mutant CFTR and the protein NHERF1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underpin the development of a cystic fibrosis (Cf) disease.
the molecular mechanisms of cystic fibrosis (cf).
developing a new class of CFTR corrector molecules that can be used to treat CF patients with the ΔF508 mutation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NHERF1 binding is a determinant of functional CFTR rescue and stabilization.
the CFTR-correctors are not simply "correctors" of the misfolded mutant CFTR protein but also "stabilizers" of rescued mutant CFTR.
the CFTR corrector, VX-809, stabilizes the interaction between CFTR and NHERF1, which leads to an increase in the stability of the CFTR channel at the plasma membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interaction of the CFTR channel protein with NHERF1 plays a critical role in the stabilization of the rescued ΔF508-CFTR mutant channel protein in the cell membrane and that this interaction is enhanced by the CFTR corrector drug VX-809.

we show that the rescue of the ΔF-508 mutant CFTR channel protein by VX-809 involves the formation of a macromolecular complex between CFTR and NHERF1, and that this interaction is a determinant in the stabilization of ΔF-508 CFTR at and/or within the plasma membrane.
VX-809 stabilizes ΔF508 CF TR by enhancing its interaction with the scaffolding protein NHERF1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated the importance of protein-protein interaction in stabilizing mutant CFTR at cell surface and that the stabilization can be achieved by small molecules.
the stabilization of the interaction between the CFTR mutant channel and its binding partners is a determinant of functional efficiency.

the interaction between the mutant CFTR channel and the scaffolding protein NHERF1 is a determinant of CFTR function, and this interaction is stabilized by VX-809, which is currently in clinical trials as a CFTR corrector.
